items.claim: The row's ketiv/qere disclosure at Prov.21.29 mislabels the second variant word as “the pronoun”; the affected word is the noun “way” carrying a pronominal suffix (ketiv plural / qere singular), not a free-standing pronoun.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.29 byte text: the closing clause reads ‘יכין יָבִ֬ין דרכיו דַּרְכּֽוֹ’ (byte tier, collate.py GREEN). pmarks_Prov.json kq confirms exactly 2 ketiv/qere notes at Prov.21.29, matching the row's count of two. The first pair (יכין ketiv / יָבִ֬ין qere) is a verb, correctly described as such. The second pair (דרכיו ketiv, plural / דַּרְכּֽוֹ qere, singular) is the noun for ‘way’ with a possessive suffix, not a pronoun in its own right; the row's phrase ‘the verb and pronoun of that closing clause’ names the wrong part of speech for the second object.

items.claim: All six Hebrew quotes in the row collate at byte tier, the divrei-hakhamim phrase is correctly placed in-verse rather than as a header, and the 22:20 ketiv/qere crux is disclosed without being resolved, as required.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.22.17 (‘הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֭שְׁמַע דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים וְ֝לִבְּךָ֗ תָּשִׁ֥ית לְדַעְתִּֽי’) is 8 words; the phrase ‘דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים’ occupies words 4-5, after the double attention-imperative (words 1-3) and before the purpose clause that follows (words 6-8) -- a genuine mid-verse position, not verse-initial. This matches the book-wide pattern: at oshb:Prov.1.6 the same phrase ‘דִּבְרֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים’ also sits at words 4-5 of a 6-word verse, non-initial there too, and prov_device_inventory.json confirms these are the only 2 book-wide sites for the phrase. The 22:20 quote (qere form) collates at byte tier; the row explicitly reports the ketiv/qere numeral-vs-rank crux as unresolved (confidence medium_low), matching the writer's own low-confidence hold rather than silently picking a reading. The claimed petuchah/pe at 22:21 matches pmarks_Prov.json exactly (PE, not conflated with SAMEKH). check_marks.py and citation_sweep.py both return GREEN with zero flags on this row.
